world_rules: The interpreter's rendering enters the record as verbatim; the court cannot check the hill dialect against her.
A witness and the interpreter may not confer; anything passing between them off the record is neither evidence nor permitted.
The charge turns on a single act years ago; the only witness who could place the accused there is dead.
The hill-dialect verb for what happened at the sluice holds two senses — to be led, and to lead — parted only by breath and by the one who carries it across.
locations: the witness corridor behind the chamber
objects: the water jug on the witness rail
